author: David Reed
summary: Tier 2 can no longer be talked out of a denial by its own confidence. The Medical Director branch discarded the agent's status and recomputed it from the confidence score alone, so a denial held with high conviction was rewritten into an autonomous approval while the same denial held with less conviction went to a human. Tier 2 now applies Tier 1's routing rule, which requires both high confidence and an AUTO_APPROVED status before granting autonomy.

changes.description: Route the Tier-2 Medical Director outcome through select_confidence_branch instead of a confidence-only threshold, so the agent's determination decides the outcome and confidence only gates whether an approval may be autonomous.
changes.failure_pattern: The Medical Director Agent denies a case and is confident about it, and the system issues an autonomous approval. The same denial held with less conviction routes to a human, so lowering the agent's certainty made the system safer.
changes.root_cause: _run_medical_director assigned status from confidence alone: >= auto_approve_confidence_threshold set AUTO_APPROVED, anything else set IN_REVIEW. That reads confidence_score as 'confidence the request should be approved'. The agent produces it as 'confidence in the determination it just made' -- a different quantity that agrees with the first only when the determination happens to be an approval. On a denial the two invert. Tier 1 never had this defect: select_confidence_branch requires confidence >= threshold AND status == AUTO_APPROVED. The rule was restated at Tier 2 instead of reused, and the restatement dropped the status conjunct.

evidence.note: 8 of 16 tests fail. A DENIED decision at confidence 0.95, 0.97, 0.99 and 1.0 each returns AUTO_APPROVED. INFORMATION_NEEDED and PENDING at 0.99 also return AUTO_APPROVED -- high confidence in 'I need more information' was read as support for approving.
Tier 1's rule includes the status conjunct the Tier-2 branch omitted, so the two tiers disagreed about what a confident denial means.
GC-035 is a corpus case that denies at 0.96 with a cited basis and an appeal pathway, establishing that a confident denial is a real outcome this system produces and not a hypothetical.

changes.why_this_component: The defect is in the orchestrator's policy application, not in the agent's clinical reasoning -- the agent reached the right determination and the branch overwrote it. Reusing select_confidence_branch rather than adding a second correct rule means the two tiers cannot drift apart again, which is how this arose. A prompt-level instruction could not have helped: the agent already denied, and its status was discarded afterwards.
changes.rollback_plan: git revert the commit. Reverting restores the confidence-only assignment and reopens autonomous approval of denied cases, so it should only be done alongside an alternative fix.

baseline.claim: The Tier-2 branch assigned status from confidence alone, so a Medical Director decision of DENIED at or above the auto-approve threshold was returned as AUTO_APPROVED, and any non-approval status at high confidence was likewise returned as AUTO_APPROVED.
baseline.verified_by: Run tests/unit/test_tier2_denial_is_final.py against the orchestrator at harness-iter-25, with the Medical Director agent mocked to return a chosen (status, confidence) pair.
baseline.result: 8 failed, 5 passed. DENIED at 0.95/0.97/0.99/1.0 -> AUTO_APPROVED; DENIED at 0.55 -> IN_REVIEW; IN_REVIEW, INFORMATION_NEEDED and PENDING at 0.99 -> AUTO_APPROVED. After the fix: 16 passed. Full deterministic suite 1058 passed, 6 skipped, confirming nothing else depended on the old behaviour.
